claims.text: Turmoil rose again amongst the group when Gorbag and Shagrat disagreed with what they had to do with the prisoner. Shagrat's orders from above were simple: all personal effects were to be sent to Barad-dûr. Shagrat did not trust many of his own troops, and none of Gorbag's, so he locked up the prisoner in the top chamber of the Tower of Cirith Ungol.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, The Lord of the Rings, The Two Towers, "The Choices of Master Samwise", pp. 735-42

claims.text: Gorbag coveted the Mithril-coat Frodo wore and attempted to usurp Shagrat's rule, but lost to Shagrat's superior numbers. Soon, Gorbag's faction was pressed back. Shagrat eventually killed Gorbag and ran off to Sauron with the prisoner's belongings. He reached Barad-dûr three days later, on 17 March. After Shagrat brought him the news and items, Sauron slew him.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, The Lord of the Rings, The Return of the King, "The Tower of Cirith Ungol", pp. 905-7; J.R.R. Tolkien, The Lord of the Rings, Appendix B, "The Great Years", p. 1094; J.R.R. Tolkien, "Time-scheme for The Lord of the Rings"(Marquette MSS 4/2/18) in Wayne G. Hammond and Christina Scull (eds), The Lord of the Rings: A Reader's Companion,"The Land of Shadow", p. 608
